findings.current: بھیجنے کے لیے کمپیوٹر سے منسلک ہوں۔
findings.replacement: بھیجنے کے لیے کمپیوٹر سے منسلک ہو جائیں۔
findings.why: ‘ہوں’ is ہونا's 1st-person/3rd-plural subjunctive; with no subject in the sentence the reader supplies ‘I’, so the line reads “so that I be connected”, not “Connect …”. Core does use this shape where the subject is present (‘تجاویز آن ہوں’), which is why it looks plausible — but a directive to آپ needs the polite imperative. ‘ہو جائیں’ keeps the intransitive verb core already uses for connection state (‘دوبارہ منسلک ہو رہا ہے…’) and matches Hindi’s shipped imperative (‘कंप्यूटर से कनेक्ट करें’). Shorter alternative if the composer slot is tight: «بھیجنے کے لیے کمپیوٹر جوڑیں۔» (29 cells, core’s pairing verb).
findings.evidence: rendered before/after through parseMessage+formatMessage in audit.log; Hindi sibling fr/hi comparison

findings.current: ذیلی ایجنٹس پھیلانے کے لیے متوازی کام مانگیں
findings.replacement: ذیلی ایجنٹس کو پھیلانے کے لیے متوازی کام مانگیں
findings.why: پھیلانا is transitive; without ‘کو’ the fragment reads like spreading objects rather than the agents fanning out. With ‘کو’ it is 47 characters, one under TIP_CHAR_BUDGET=48.

‘سمیت’ is officialese/Persianised (core uses it only in technical lists); a chat chip reads better with the everyday construction. Trade-off: 23 characters, 1 over the translator’s own 22 longest — needs the same width check the translator already runs; the current string is acceptable if that budget is tight.
findings.evidence: chip lengths measured; Hindi shipped uses ‘सारांश के साथ’

findings.current: قطار کے پیغامات بھیجنے کے لیے دوبارہ کوشش کریں
findings.why: ‘queued messages’ renders as ‘قطار کے پیغامات’ in the two status rows and ‘قطار میں لگے پیغامات’ in the sheet and its buttons — same noun, two forms, one screen. Both are grammatical and the short form serves the row width; recorded rather than required.

findings.replacement: شروع ہونے کی تصدیق نہیں ہوئی
findings.why: Terse nominal sentence without ہوئی; acceptable as a status label, fuller form reads smoother.
